Sentence (English): I'm happy with how quiet it is, and how clean it gets the items being washed.
Comments (English): [ Decent dishwasher, but missing features ] || ---------------- || I'm happy with how quiet it is, and how clean it gets the items being washed. It's great for tall glasses- the middle rack has enough distance from the top rack that I can wash even really tall glasses and jars without having to lower the rack. Excellent. It's not so good for small glasses or stemware- I wish it had a set of arms that would clip to the side of the rack and swing down to support the stems of wine glasses (an old dishwasher I had decades ago had this; it's a great feature). Considering the unit's four-digit price, it should have them. The user guide talks about sliding bowl tines, fold down tines, and stemware holders, but my unit has none of these things. The tines are such that only a few balloon wine glasses can be placed in the rack, and the plastic rack raise/lower mechanism crowds them, reducing the number of glasses that can be put in. The middle rack's spacing of horizontal supports/wires is so wide that it's hard to put lots of smaller glasses (like 5 oz snifters) in without them trying to tip over. The top rack could be a smidgen deeper (or lower) to accommodate thicker utensils like ladles, scrapers, bigger spoons. As I use it more, I may find ways of supporting the items I wash most often. The bottom rack basket is useful, but I find I don't use the top lids of it- The holes in the lids don't accommodate anything I'd poke through them. So I'll just leave the lids off. Would I recommend this unit? Maybe.

Sentence (English): My prior dishwasher displayed a green light if the load was done and clean.
Comments (English): [ The "finshed" screen is what I wanted ] || ---------------- || My prior dishwasher displayed a green light if the load was done and clean. Once you opened the dishwasher, the green light turned off. Thus, if you opened the dishwasher and didn't have time to unload it, then the green light would turn off and the next family member might load dirty dishes into a clean load. I cared a lot about the way this dishwasher would behave when the load was finished. Here is what happens:When the washer finishes, the screen displays "Finished" until you open the dishwasher. Once you open the diswasher, the screen will continue to display "Finished" until you close the dishwasher completely again or turn off the dishwasher. This means you can open the dishwasher, remove a clean item, allow the springs to keep the door amost entirely closed, and the screen will still display "Finished" to your other family members until someone unloads the washer or until someone bumps the dishwasher door closed. If you bump the door closed the screen will display "Please start dishwasher." If you reopen the door, the screen will display a blank line assuming you are about to start a new load from scratch given that you haven't yet turned off the dishwasher. In many alternative makes and models I was considering, I was finding that the finished light, if offered, would do things like turn off after 3 hours. That wouldn't help clearify the status of the dishes to a busy household. Other comments:The dishwasher is very quite.I like that the plate racks have a slight angle in the bottom tray as opposed to a completely vertical post like my old washer that resulted in domino plates when a plate tipped over.I liked the utencil drawer in my old LG slightly more for one OCD reason, the utencils sat in nice vertically aligned rows. With all the notches in the 3rd utencil rack, the utencils tend to end up sitting at slight angles to one another as opposed to perfectly aligned.

Once you open the diswasher, the screen will continue to display "Finished" until you close the dishwasher completely again or turn off the dishwasher. This means you can open the dishwasher, remove a clean item, allow the springs to keep the door amost entirely closed, and the screen will still display "Finished" to your other family members until someone unloads the washer or until someone bumps the dishwasher door closed. If you bump the door closed the screen will display "Please start dishwasher." If you reopen the door, the screen will display a blank line assuming you are about to start a new load from scratch given that you haven't yet turned off the dishwasher. In many alternative makes and models I was considering, I was finding that the finished light, if offered, would do things like turn off after 3 hours. That wouldn't help clearify the status of the dishes to a busy household. Other comments: The dishwasher is very quite. I like that the plate racks have a slight angle in the bottom tray as opposed to a completely vertical post like my old washer that resulted in domino plates when a plate tipped over. I liked the utencil drawer in my old LG slightly more for one OCD reason, the utencils sat in nice vertically aligned rows. With all the notches in the 3rd utencil rack, the utencils tend to end up sitting at slight angles to one another as opposed to perfectly aligned.

Only caveat, the 3rd rack cutlery holder has been changed on all models, and the small insert is pretty useless; it wobbles, and barely holds a meal's worth of cutlery. We purchased a part to increase capacity; not only did it not fit correctly, returning the part actually cost more than the part itself! (25% "restocking" fee and $58 postage). We did find we could order a replacement rack, and did so for an additional $70, it took all of 2 minutes to install. Seriously, Bosch, if it ain't broke, don't fix it, there was no need for this change.

Comments (English): [ Over Rated ] || ---------------- || I have to honestly say that this is by far one of the poorest designed dishwashers I have ever owned, and in my 70+ years I have owned quite a few. To be more specific my first issue is with the lower rack layout. With half the rack going in one direction and the other half running ninety degrees to that it makes loading the dishes very awkward. Sentence (English): This is my second Bosch dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Very Quiet and Sparkling Clean ] || ---------------- || This is my second Bosch dishwasher. I decided to stick with Bosch because the first one lasted for 12+ years! It outlasted all other appliances (TV, driers, washers) that was installed the same time during a major home renovation. Definitely worth the extra dollars. This machine is super quiet! Will give you sparkling clean dishes on every wash. This machine is also quite easy to install. If you are replacing an old one like i did, you will likely do the following 2 changes to the existing configuration. I had to convert the power source to a 20 amp/120V GFCI outlet from a direct switch. Newer dishwasher now have the 3 prong power cords. I also had to replace the old copper line with the newer metal braided dishwasher 3/8s line. I connected the the remaining copper line still connected to the shut off valve and the new line using a 3/8 OD Compression connector. (see third photo). The connector only cost 7$. All this work avoided expensive installation costs!

Also the part where the tines are shorter are just not good for anything, at least not what I cook with…. However they might work better if they were farther apart. Getting cookie sheets, Pyrex dishes or pans and lids to stand up and wash? Hahaha … forget it. You will be using space in between the time segments thank goodness for the top sprayer arm when it comes to washing your cookware. The sprayer arms on top and bottom work great, the wheels are really nice, easy rolling and quick connect is so easy. These are important to me because we have to roll the dishwasher over just a bit to connect and of course connect the water as well, and easy peasy! Overall pretty satisfied.

Sentence (English): Model reviewed: Bosch SHXM78Z55N/22.
Comments (English): [ SHXM78Z55N/22 review ] || ---------------- || Model reviewed: Bosch SHXM78Z55N/22. Purchased at and delivered by Best Buy. Bottom line first: We like this dishwasher and recommend it to others. Details: We bought this dishwasher based upon on-line reviews and the quality of the previous Bosch dishwasher we owned for 11 years. We've had this machine for 6 weeks now. It is quiet, cleans well and it looks good. Some reviewers complained of dishes still wet after wash. We start the machine at bedtime and use the Crystal Dry option. The dishes are dry and clean in the morning. I did my own installation (DIY) and the only problem I encountered was that the machine is a bit longer than the unit it replaced, which required relocation of the electrical outlet behind the dishwasher. I suspected this going in, so it came as no surprise. If you decide to install yourself, you should have moderate DIY mechanical, electrical and drywall skills. And, patience in working under sink and counters. The unit was delivered un-damaged. There was a loose machine screw present lying in the bottom of the packaging pallet. I was unable to determine where it came from. Hopefully this is not an issue down line. Installation of the dishwasher required purchase of an optional installation kit, which provided water supply hose and various plumbing fittings. This kit also included another power cord with standard three prong plug on one end and bare tinned wires on the other end. The washer already includes a power cord with standard three prong on one end and female connector that mates with the dishwasher on the other end. Also included with the dishwasher was a separate power cord with junction box that allows the installer to connect the dishwasher directly to house wiring where no receptacle exists. In my opinion I think they got the kit options backwards. The dishwasher should come standard with the water hose and fittings. I can't imagine few or any situations where a standard electrical receptacle is not already present, thus making the two other power cords and junction box superfluous. Local hardware stores have standard electrical boxes and receptacles available and for probably less money. In closing, we are completely satisfied with our purchase.

Details: We bought this dishwasher based upon on-line reviews and the quality of the previous Bosch dishwasher we owned for 11 years. We've had this machine for 6 weeks now. It is quiet, cleans well and it looks good. Some reviewers complained of dishes still wet after wash. We start the machine at bedtime and use the Crystal Dry option. The dishes are dry and clean in the morning. I did my own installation (DIY) and the only problem I encountered was that the machine is a bit longer than the unit it replaced, which required relocation of the electrical outlet behind the dishwasher. I suspected this going in, so it came as no surprise. If you decide to install yourself, you should have moderate DIY mechanical, electrical and drywall skills. And, patience in working under sink and counters. The unit was delivered un-damaged. There was a loose machine screw present lying in the bottom of the packaging pallet. I was unable to determine where it came from. Hopefully this is not an issue down line. Installation of the dishwasher required purchase of an optional installation kit, which provided water supply hose and various plumbing fittings. This kit also included another power cord with standard three prong plug on one end and bare tinned wires on the other end. The washer already includes a power cord with standard three prong on one end and female connector that mates with the dishwasher on the other end. Also included with the dishwasher was a separate power cord with junction box that allows the installer to connect the dishwasher directly to house wiring where no receptacle exists. In my opinion I think they got the kit options backwards. The dishwasher should come standard with the water hose and fittings. I can't imagine few or any situations where a standard electrical receptacle is not already present, thus making the two other power cords and junction box superfluous. Local hardware stores have standard electrical boxes and receptacles available and for probably less money. In closing, we are completely satisfied with our purchase.

I'm a little worried now because I just read a review about wheels melting and the front rusting. Wish me luck!

Sentence (English): ProDry feature was main reason we bought this model.
Comments (English): [ ProDry is a joke and so is the KitchenAid brand ] || ---------------- || ProDry feature was main reason we bought this model. Unit cleans but don't expect it to dry anything--unless you are installing on demand hot water in extremely close proximity to unit. KitchenAid Customer Service--though courteous--says it's not their problem and has no solution. So don't believe the advertisements, the \"Consumer Reviews,\" or any sales rep. Heck even the repair technician said he had to sign a non-disclosure with the company in order to receive repair calls. He came out--less than a year after purchase--and I was expected to pay the service fee because they said the unit wasn't faulty, that my water wasn't hot enough--when he recorded 121F out of the faucet next to unit. He said if you don't have internal water temps at a minimum of 90F in less than a minute to your dishwasher the unit defaults and doesn't heat at all. This was the second KitchenAid dishwasher I've owned and the last product manufactured by this company I will ever purchase in my lifetime. They don't build the product to function as advertise in an average American home. Extremely disappointed.

Sentence (English): I'm glad I got this on sale over Memorial Day and didn't pay full price.
Comments (English): [ Meh. Be prepared to hand dry. ] || ---------------- || I'm glad I got this on sale over Memorial Day and didn't pay full price. It cleans ok (I pre-rinse all of my dishes well before loading, so hard to say how it does with truly dirty dishes). My main issue is that it doesn't dry my dishes. I've added rinse-aid, chosen the “extended dry” cycle and still, the inside door is wet, as are my dishes. Also, came with zero instructions, so had to look on YouTube to figure out how the cycles work. Oh, and if you use the “quick wash” (1 hour) cycle, you don't have the option of sani-rinse, high temp wash or the extended dry cycles, so you're looking at it running for over 3 hours with any of the other cycles. On the plus side, it's an extremely quiet machine.

I would recommend buying it, but NOT from Costco, at least in Bay Area. Better think about it again. The public review of this company is notorious, I hope I knew it, and Costco, you should reveal the service provide before the checkout. The installer was so unprofessional and careless, I heard the bang bang noise coming from the my kitchen, he was trying to put things in place simply by brutal force. My countertop was broken, into pieces. And me, the customer, was then like the tennis ball hit back and forth by 2 players, Pac West and Costco. And then left in the middle of the court, no one cares. I called both parties, contractor and Costco, but all ended resultless and no help. The contractor reacted rudely and nonsense-ly and hung up my calls and denied the damage(they said my countertop was broken before the installation, right after I sent them photo proofs), the Costco online customer service initially told me to reach out to the contractor and told me to be patient, and started to NOT reply any of my inquiries for months(and I think they decided to not reply once I ask them to escalate the case, LOL). Both parties decided to stay in silent and just leave the customer stuck there with broken properties. What nonsense! Never been in a such unpleasant scenario before, and the damage claim requires to leave the scene as it is until inspection is done, so everyday I will see my damaged countertop, which is not a happy thing to see, waiting to be reached out for inspection or whatever next step is, which never happened. One Costco representative/agent initially told me to I should talk with Pac West for resolution because it is my contractor, I argued back it is Costco's contractor because I never signed contract with them and don't even know the name before checkout. And no reply since then. The Costco online order customer service is the worst I ever seen. I was expecting it to be same as good as in warehouse, but that is not the case. Maybe you feel you would be the lucky guy and won't experience the same stated in the bad reviews like mine or all posted by others. Actually I was one of the guys. I spent a lot every year in warehouse as well as Costco online, but this is the first purchase that requires a complex installation, and feel very disappointed. This is a long story, but a sad story.

I rinse everything well and run the hot water for several minutes to ensure that it is hot enough to clean properly but it doesn't make a difference. We were also told that there was a quick cycle but the quick cycle is 1hr 44 minutes and you have to put the extra dry cycle on with it…and there are still wet. Will probably bite the bullet and give this away and buy a higher end dishwasher.

Comments (English): [ The third rack is a complete game-changer! ] || ---------------- || I've been using this machine for about three weeks, and cannot say enough good about it. When we needed to replace our very old luxury brand dishwasher, we trusted the Whirlpool name and the good reviews. Going to look at various models available at my local Lowe's, I saw this one that also included a third rack for items like big cooking utensils, plastic lids, and small glasses. What a difference this makes! The dishwasher is deeper than usual in the floor (by a couple of inches), making room for that top rack, and it also has a fully adjustable second rack for larger pans and silverware baskets that come apart for fitting into different configurations if needed. It does a very good job cleaning everything (especially if I set it to "sensor" so that it decides how hot and how forceful the water needs to be based on the condition of the dishes). It also dries very well, with the one exception of plastic lids. However, if it heated enough to completely dry those , they would probably melt, so all in all I am thrilled with the performance.

Sentence (English): I've only had this a few weeks, maybe just over a month, but I really enjoy it.
Comments (English): [ Doing great so far ] || ---------------- || I've only had this a few weeks, maybe just over a month, but I really enjoy it. The capacity is great, install was easy (on the dishwasher side -my house plumbing was another story) and the wash cycles really get dishes clean and the drying really gets the items dry, even plastic. I did upgrade from a 39 year old dishwasher so I'm pretty sure I would have been happy with almost anything. In particular, I really like the flexibility of the tines that hold up the dishes, you can put up or lay down sections of the tines in a variety of ways to support different dishes. I also like the easy way to adjust the height of the middle rack and the zone control function. These things really help with washing small loads or big/awkward items appropriately. The third tray is amazing, I don't know that it's particularly amazing over other similar dishwashers, but I love it for small items like cutlery, lids, etc.

Comments (English): [ So disappointed ] || ---------------- || I ordered this online from Home Depot after seeing it at the store. It was not in stock in the location. I used the number on the sign, the price was the same as in the store, and yet, it was a different dishwasher that I ordered. It was for a kitchen remodel, so we waiting until it was time to install it to open it. It has none of the features I expected: No third level, no cup rack, the tines are for the most part not adjustable, and there are no stemware holders, all things featured in the dishwasher at Home Depot and the reason I bought it. I am truly disappointed and stuck with a dishwasher I will hate for a long time. This is, essentially, the most basic model of dishwasher you can imagine. At least it's quiet. Sentence (English): We purchased ours gently used because our old dishwasher broke, and I have to say I dislike it.
Comments (English): [ Solidly meh. ] || ---------------- || We purchased ours gently used because our old dishwasher broke, and I have to say I dislike it. The capacity is definitely far smaller than our previous portable dishwasher, and because none of the prongs have bowl-shaped cutouts for them to sit correctly it fits maybe half of the bowls our old model did; bowls must be rather artfully arranged around your other dishes or, if you load it according to their directions, will take up a huge amount of space. The first time I tried to put in a family's worth of breakfast cereal bowls, juice glasses and coffee mugs wanted to scream.The utensil rack is similarly precious. It is sturdy, solid moulded plastic which is great for forks/knives/spoons but useless for anything else we used to use our old one for (infant bottle parts, spatulas, small Tupperware lids, water bottle lids etc). These small parts we used to put in the utensil area to avoid them being blown around by the water pressure must all be washed by hand now.The cycle buttons are clear and easy to use. but the second you close the door they are 100% impossible to see. What is the point of this? I guess it looks nice aesthetically but you can't tell where you are in a wash cycle without opening the door! It washes and dries fine, and is relatively quiet. Those are the pluses.We bought this out of necessity, have had it for a few days and we cannot wait to save up for something better.

Sentence (English): My wife bought two KDTM704KPS dishwashers today.
Comments (English): [ Racks still have problems - not durable ] || ---------------- || My wife bought two KDTM704KPS dishwashers today. One to replace our KDTM404ESS3 and the second for our new pantry. Wish I had looked inside before starting installation. I have installed 8 dishwashers over the years. Not an expert but know how to do it. During installation the rail lock tab on the upper rack broke. I was just looking at it trying to remember how the lock mechanism works and saw a hairline crack. When I pushed on the lock tab to release the rack it felt weak. I relooked at the hairline crack and saw that it had widened. Having had rack problems with the KDTM404 (pump failed in 4th year and had broken racks) I was dismayed to see they are still using plastic tabs to hold the 2nd and new third racks on the new 704. These weight holding tabs and locks are headed for failure again. I was super careful when I pushed the VERY HARD TO FIND lock tabs on the racks. But one broke nevertheless. Removing the second rack is required under installation step 40 but the INADEQUATE instructions on how to remove the rack are somewhat found on Page 3. The button you need to push is hard to find, is hard to push and one of the four broke with minimal pushing. It was also difficult to reinstall the racks. Unfortunately these are more or less the same racks that were on the KDTM404. I fully anticipate having to modify these racks by adding stainless steel bolts with nylock nuts within a few years. Also had a problem with the middle rack. When I opened the door for the first time the height adjustment RED push down button on the right was stuck in an inoperable position. After fussing with it I discovered that sliding a screwdriver up into a slot in the bottom would release it. But the point is: The average homeowner can easily push the button in too far causing the button to stick and not know how to fix it. Why on earth would your engineering team design it for a high likelihood of customer dissatisfaction? Also…make your rack holding tabs out of metal rather than easy to break plastic. All the bells and whistles in the racks are just dandy but if the essential holding parts are weak and break you are producing customer disatisfaction. Cleaning on our 404 was good until $500 pump gave out after 4 years of daily use. Hopefully that doesn't happen on the 704. Kind of dreading the upcoming rack problems and questioning….should I return the 2nd one? Warranty claim will be incoming on the broken rack on the first one. But that doesn't solve the poor design issues on the racks that will cause me future grief.

Sentence (English): I needed a dishwasher quickly to replace an old Kenmore, but didn't want to spend a lot of money, as we'll be moving soon.
Comments (English): [ No frills dishwasher ] || ---------------- || I needed a dishwasher quickly to replace an old Kenmore, but didn't want to spend a lot of money, as we'll be moving soon. With the holiday sale bringing this one into my budget range, I bought it after reading good reviews. It wasn't in stock so had to be ordered, which meant I didn't get to see or touch it till we picked it up. The website information lead me to believe that this model had a removable tray on the upper silverware rack, as well as a fold down shelf on the middle rack. Not true. This is as basic, no frills as it gets. There are only basic cycles. However, it does a good job of cleaning and drying the dishes. The cycle is long - over 3 hours! I let it run at night. It's quiet and we can't hear it running anywhere except the kitchen. If I wasn't moving, I would have invested in a machine with more options that I use and like. I can't complain - I was shopping for price. As is, I'd consider this an adequate machine for the sale price I paid.

Sentence (English): We bought this to replace a Samsung that was only a few months old.
Comments (English): [ Excellent Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || We bought this to replace a Samsung that was only a few months old. Somehow the dishes in the Samsung came out dirtier than they went in. We were hesitant buying a new dishwasher but with all of the positive reviews and the features we decided to make the purchase. The spinning glass washer on the third rack works great and the mid rack that can hold large countertop mixer bowls is a big plus when baking. The racks are spaced well for all kinds and shapes of dishes. We run it at least once a day, often twice to accommodate the dish load of our family of 6. We have found using a Finish dish tablet along with a little liquid for the pre-wash gives us the best results. Even with the more premium price tag we find it has been worth the money.

In fact, there are water droplets hanging on the inner wall, and there are more water droplets on the shelf, which will drip onto the bowl. There is a function on the panel called air-drying. Besides, the cleaning ability is used in the daily mode, 78 minutes, and I feel that 3 times out of 10 times, the washing is not clean. For example, there will be a lot of residue in the bowl of steamed eggs. Finally, let me talk about a small problem. It is not convenient enough to close the door with two hands.
